Welcome to our school
St Mary’s C.E. Primary School is a diverse and inclusive two form entry primary school with a Nursery, situated in Finchley Central.
Our school has a strong Christian ethos, underpinned by the Christian values of Compassion, Endurance, Reverence, Hope, Service and Thankfulness. If you would like to visit us please call the school office.
Nursery
Please click to find out more about what we offer and how nursery provision is run.
Curriculum
All you need to know about curriculum and subjects we learn at St.Mary's CE.
SEND & INCUSION
Please take a look what support we provide to overcome barriers to learning.
Extra-Curricular
Please click to see what we are able to offer to our children beyond classroom.
Who are we?
St Mary’s has a strong and distinctive Christian ethos and vision, yet we remain inclusive of all children in our community, including those with different faiths and those of no faith.
Our vision, values and the ‘Big Ideas’ we promote in the curriculum are universal, ensuring that they hold value and meaning for all our children, families and staff.
Our school logo is a good way to explain ‘Who are we?’, because it says a great deal about our school.
There are six elements to highlight, all embedded in our daily provision:
Centre Cross, Centre Star, Scallop Shell, Bishop’s Mitre, Fleur de Lis and A Finch.
Our logo explained
Centre Cross – A symbol of our Christian identity as a schoolOur Christian vision, values and curriculum ‘Big Ideas’ permeate the school at all levels, while recognising that we serve the entire community, Christian or otherwise.
Centre Star – Illustrates our vision for every child to have the chance to shine.Everybody (adults and children) gets the opportunity to shine and we celebrate the unique skills and achievement of each person.Our provision will help all children to flourish (shine) physically, emotionally, academically and spiritually.
Scallop Shell – Symbol or Baptism and Pilgrimage – Our journey through life.Every child is unique and therefore their journey through life and how they develop is equally unique. Every child will learn and grow in their own may, while developing in their learning and in their personal life.
Bishop’s Mitre – It shows the link to our connection with the Church of England.The school preserves and develops its religious character in accordance with the principles of the Church of England and in partnership with the Church at parish and diocesan level, ensuring that all children are included in every part of our provision.
Fleur de Lis – Symbol for Mary (our patron saint).The Fleur de Lis (Lily Flower), represents purity which is associated with the Virgin Mary. Mary was called by God to do a special job, giving birth to Jesus, and she accepted it. It reminds us that we all have calling, a special job, and that in fulfilling it, God is always with us.
A Finch – Our school represents everybody in the community of Finchley.All children are welcome and valued in our school, because we serve our local community in its entirety. We celebrate our diversity and beliefs, and we ensure that our Christian values of compassion and service extend to everybody we encounter.In addition, our British Values of Respect and Individual Liberty are firmly embedded. Our Christian and British values is promoted in our curriculum and evident in our relationships in school.
Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and all people.(Luke 2:52)
Just like Jesus, we recognize the journey each of us are on, growing in our learning and in our personal development. Our provision at school aims to make the best possible use of every opportunity to:

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Christian Ethos, Vision and Values – St Mary’s C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Inspirational Bible Text
Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and all people. – Luke 2:52
St Mary’s is a Church of England school and is therefore required to have a clear Christian ethos.
This ethos is demonstrated in the way the school teaches the pupils and how we interact with each other in the school community. It also permeates our provision in all areas, while remaining inclusive of all our children and families.
Our Vision summarises the ultimate aims we have for our children, while our Christian values serves as a way children and adults can put our vision in action. The curriculum Big Ideas are designed to ensure that we embed our visions and values through the curriculum we teach.
Recognising its historic foundation, the school will preserve and develop its religious character in accordance with the principles of the Church of England and in partnership with the Church at parish and diocesan level.
The school aims to serve its community by providing an education of the highest quality within the context of Christian beliefs and practice. It encourages an understanding of the meaning and significance of faith, and promotes Christian values through the experience it offers to all its pupils. Taken from Instrument of Government
Our Vision flows from the inspirational Bible text and consist of four pillars:
Deliver educational excellence and foster life-long love of learning.
Build strong personal and community relationship through Christian values.
Help children and adults flourish and fulfill their God given potential.
Provide a welcoming, safe and inclusive Christian environment.
At St Mary’s, Christian values are at the heart of our school’s vision. Through our faith in God, who is Father, Son and Holy Spirit, we ensure that our values embrace the whole school community and have a commitment to every child achieving their God-given potential, regardless of ability, age, gender, faith, language, race or culture.
When we face challenging situations, we show perseverance and patience, and the resilience and courage to achieve our goals. Click on the link for the Christian basis for the endurance value.
We use all our gifts to serve others generously in love, humility and respect, trying to become servant leaders like Jesus. Click on the link for the Christian basis for the service value.
We marvel at creation and the diversity within it and we work together to make this world a better place, treating each person as a unique individual and caring for and honoring the whole of creation. Click on the link for the Christian basis for the reverence value.
We are resilient and steadfast in our school and in the world, believing and working for a world of peace, justice and unity. Click on the link for the Christian basis for the hope value.
We care for those who share our school and those less fortunate in the world, showing empathy, love and kindness. Click on the link for the Christian basis for the compassion value.
We live lives full of gratitude for all that we have and all that others have done for us, and show this through our words and deeds. Click on the link for the Christian basis for the thankfulness value.
Our Curriculum ‘Big Ideas’
Each unit of work in our curriculum is linked to a Big Idea which helps us to embed our Values and Vision in our learning from the National Curriculum. These are as follows:

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values – St Mary’s C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
At St. Mary’s Church of England School, and in accordance with the Department for Education requirements, we aim to actively promote British Values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain.
British Values are introduced, discussed and lived out through our values of Hope, Reverence, Service and Compassion. Our curriculum also provides opportunities to promote these values through learning in RE, PSHE and other units in the broader curriculum. There are also times when we specifically learn about each of the British Values, often through our daily act of worship or British Values week.
The school actively promotes the need to treat all people with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its laws.
The British Values are:
Democracy
The rule of law
Individual liberty

pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship – St Mary’s C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
What is Collective Worship?
Collective worship is a sacred and significant time of each school day, where we gather together as a whole school family. It is the unique heartbeat of the school and is offered as part of a wider opportunity for pupils and adults to encounter faith by engaging in conversations about God, both as individuals and together. All acts of worship in church schools are (must be) Christian in character.
Collective worship strengthens and supports the Christian identity of our school and reaffirms our Christian vision and associated values of Endurance, Service, Hope, Reverence, Thankfulness and Compassion.
Collective worship and Religious Education (RE) are not the same. The law requires both RE and collective worship to take place in school, but at different times. The difference is that worship is concerned with celebration of, and reflective responses to, religious themes whereas RE involves study of them as an academic subject.
Inclusive, Invitational, and Inspiring
Inclusive: In St Mary’s, pupils and adults can expect to encounter worship that is inclusive of, and fully accessible to all. We understand that many pupils and staff in our schools will come from homes of different faith backgrounds as well as of no faith background.
We also know that pupils will be different stages of their spiritual journey during their time in school. Pupils should be given the opportunity to think and ask questions. We will ensure that care will be taken to ensure that the language used by those facilitating worship avoids assuming faith in all those participating. It will involve meaningful contributions from them, bringing their own experience to worship.
Invitational: Pupils and adults can expect to encounter worship that is consistently invitational. There will be no compulsion to ‘do anything’. Rather, worship should provide the opportunity to engage whilst allowing the freedom of those of different faiths and no faith background to be present and to engage with integrity.
This means that there is clarity and authenticity of the Christian message at the heart of Collective Worship, but that everybody can engage at the level that they feel comfortable with. Pupils and adults will only be invited to pray if they wish to do so will invited to pray in their own way.
Inspiring: Pupils and adults can expect the worship they encounter in St Mary’s to be inspirational. Worship aims to be formational and transformational, enabling pupils and adults to ask big questions about who we are and why we do what we do. It aims to should motivate pupils and adults into action, into thinking differently and into reflecting on their and the community’s behaviour and actions.
As a result of inspirational collective worship, we want participants to be inspired to become courageous advocates of causes. It should encourage them to think searchingly about their faith, beliefs and/or philosophical convictions.
Occasionally there will be those who are uncomfortable to enter through this open door of worship in our schools and so the Church of England recognises the right of withdrawal from collective worship for those parents or pupils who wish to exercise this option.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome – St Mary’s C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
Dear Parents, Carers and Visitors
Welcome to St Mary’s Church of England Primary School’s website. We hope that you will find all the things you need to know about our wonderful school and that it will give you some insight to life at St Mary’s.
Our Biblical inspiration, from Luke 2:52, forms the foundation of our vision:
‘Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and all people’
Our children and adults Learn, Grow and Shine and their learning and development at St Mary’s takes place within a Christian atmosphere and environment where all children, regardless of their background, can flourish. We provide a caring and supportive learning environment, where we aim to (our vision):
Our vision is put into action through the teaching and living our Christian Values and the curriculum Big Ideas. You can click on the link to find out more about these.
We have a skilled and dedicated team of adults in school and they help all our children to achieve excellent academic outcomes. We also have specialist teachers delivering Music and PE. You can read more about our children’s academic achievements, by clicking on the link.
While learning remains at the forefront of what we do in school, there is so much more to our school. We offer a variety of clubs and most children are able to find something that they are interested in. We also have a breakfast and after school club to make life easier for our working parents.
Our children also take part in a wide range of sports and music events and competitions. Our children receive very good results and our school choir and peripatetic music lessons are always popular.
We also offer opportunities to grow spiritually, whether through our daily acts of worship or by making use of our prayer and reflection space. Our children show this through the way they get on with each other, their awe and wonder for God’s creation and the way they engage in charitable activities.
These are only a few of the things which add to our school being a great place for children to be, but I hope that the website will give you more information.
We would love to show you around our school and hope that we will be able to welcome you to St Mary’s soon.
Stefan Roos Executive Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Clubs and Wrap Around Care – St Mary’s C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
We feel fortunate to be able to offer our children a variety of extra-curricular clubs at our school ranging from cake decorating, gymnastics, tennis, choir, chess and art. Bookings are made directly with club organisers for each upcoming term.
Click on the link to view Clubs Booking form.
In partnership with Poolside Manor, our outstanding OFSTED-rated breakfast, after-school and holiday club providers, we are able to offer a breakfast club from 7:30am and an after-school club to 6pm.
Bookings are made directly with Poolside Manor and childcare vouchers are accepted. For further information or to book a session please contact Poolside Manor directly on 0208 349 1945 or wraparound@poolsidemanor.com and refer to the Poolside Manor website alongside the details below.
Main School (Years 1 – 6)
Available from 7.30am, held in the dining room. Your child will receive breakfast * before being taken to their classrooms at the start of the normal school day.
The costs are inclusive of breakfast (toast with spreads and cereals):
From 7.30 to 8.55am – £8.00
From 8:00 to 8.55am – £5.50
*Please note, if your child arrives after 8.40am, there may not be enough time for them to be given breakfast
Available until 6pm. Your child will be collected from their class where required (older children make their own way to Afterschool club) and will be given refreshments after their normal day at school, (not a meal replacement but aimed to help your child in their extended day).
The club is based across the dinning room and main hall as well as the children having the opportunity to go out into the playground. We have also introduced ‘homework time’ where children can carry out some of their set homework if they desire and give them more time to relax at home in the evening.
The costs are inclusive of refreshments (sandwiches, fruit and a biscuit):
Up to 1 hours – £5.00
Up to 2 hours – £8.00
Up to 2.5 hours – £10.00
More than 2.5 hours – £13.00
The clubs are staffed by high quality early years trained staff and provide a secure and stimulating environment which is age-appropriate and follows best practice from the early years foundation stage curriculum. There is a variety of exciting activities on offer, as well as opportunities for children to relax and rest. A variety of and cold food is provided.
The breakfast club is based in the main school dining room. The morning costs are inclusive of breakfast (toast with spreads and cereals):
From 7.30 to 8.55am – £8.00
From 8:00 to 8.55am – £5.50
The after school club is held in the school nursery and is exclusively for our nursery and reception children. The after school costs are inclusive of refreshments (sandwiches, fruit and a biscuit):
Up to 1 hours – £5.00
Up to 2 hours – £8.00

pageCache.pageTitle: Results and Performance data – St Mary’s C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
St. Mary’s Primary School Results – 2025
Well done to all our children and teachers for the amazing results achieved in the Summer Term 2025!
The information below compares the attainment of our pupils with local authority and national averages.
Early Years Foundation Stage
73% of pupils in Reception attained a Good Level of Development against the Early Years Framework. This is above the 2024 local authority average of 71% and the national average of 69%.
A Good Level of Development is defined as children working at the expected standard or exceeding the expected standard in the key areas of literacy, maths, physical development, communication and language and personal, social and emotional development.
Year One Phonic Screening
76% of pupils in Year One attained the expected standard in the Phonic Screening Test.
Children in Year 6 are also assessed on their knowledge and understanding of the curriculum.
The results of the SATs (tests) are reported using a scaled score, where a score of 100 represents the expected standard. The highest possible score is 120 and the lowest is 80. These tests take place for Reading, Spelling, Punctuation and Grammar (SPAG) and Maths.
Children are awarded a Teacher Assessment judgement in writing.
End of Key Stage 2 Attainment at ARE+

pageCache.text:
Statistics show that a child who is absent for one day per fortnight will have missed one year of school (190 days) by the time they leave secondary education.
The senior leader responsible for attendance is the Head of School, supported by the office team who are the first point of contact in the school for parents reporting absences.

Q5. What medical evidence is required?
Q6. Can my child attend school when he/she is on medication?
Yes, your child can come back to school as soon as he/she is feeling better. You will need to bring the medication to school (if it is prescribed to be administered 4 times a day) and complete a form allowing a member of staff to administer the medication.
Please note we have a 48-hour exclusion period following on from sickness and stomach illnesses.
Q7. What is an unacceptable reason for absence?
The school will not authorise absences for:
Please note that this list is not exhaustive.
Q8. What is an unauthorised absence?
These are absences where:
Unauthorised absences are detailed on your child’s attendance report that you will receive at the end of each year with your child’s report.
Q9. Will the school contact me if my child is absent?
Q10. Will the school monitor my child’s attendance?
Q11. Can we take family holidays during term time?
NO. Family holidays must be taken during school holidays and NOT during term time. If you take your child out of school to go on holiday without the express permission of the school, you will receive a Fixed Penalty Notice.
Q11. What are exceptional circumstances?
Exceptional circumstances are usually family emergencies or unavoidable situations for which we may require evidence. Emergencies must be notified to the school at the earliest opportunity. Other requests must be made in writing before making travel arrangements.
Parents cannot assume permission will be given. Please note that permission can only be granted for a specific period of time. Failing to follow the policy may lead to a Fixed Penalty Notice. A request for absence form can be found on the school website or from the school office.
Q12. What is a Fixed Penalty Notice?
A Fixed Penalty Notice is a fine issued by the Local Authority to parents who take their child on holiday, or out of school, during term time without the express consent of the school. Such absences are referred to the Education Welfare Team who may impose a fixed penalty fine.

Penalty notice fines, do not apply to children under the age of 5 years old and the funds that are obtained from all penalty fines, do not go to the school, they go to the local authority. If you would like further information, please see school attendance document on DfE website.
